stem: Which statement best distinguishes pH from EC in irrigation water?
choices: pH describes acidity/basicity; EC reflects bulk dissolved-ion conductivity, so they measure different properties
pH estimates the concentration of each nutrient ion, while EC primarily measures the irrigation water temperature
pH and EC describe the same solution property through different scales, so either value can substitute for the other
EC directly reports alkalinity, while pH is mainly useful for confirming the electrical reading after mixing
rationale: pH and EC describe different properties. pH indicates acidity/basicity; EC is related to the total ionic concentration and does not identify individual ions or replace pH.
